claims.assertion: This is a rider-cancelled instant booking (F4: accepted 08:40:00, cancelled by rider at 08:46:40, 6 min 40 s after matching), so the fee can only stand under NS-0's rider branch, i.e. NS-4, and the driver's arrival timeline does not by itself create a no-show charge.

Under NS-4 a rider cancellation is free only within 3 minutes of matching; the cancellation here came at 6 min 40 s, past that grace period, so NS-4 on its own makes the $6.61 cancellation fee stand (F4).

The rider's stated reason - plans changed and the driver not arrived - does not found a waiver: the record shows the driver was within 200 m of the pickup from 08:41:25 and stationary 41 m away from 08:42:00 (F2, F3).

The only ground on which the $6.61 could be refunded is a defect in the driver's arrival/waiting record, and that ground fails: the driver tapped "I'm Here" at 08:42:15 while 40 m from the pickup (within the 200 m arrival radius), stayed within 200 m for 4 min 25 s after the tap, and the cancellation came 5 min 15 s after arrival, more than 3 minutes (F2, F5, F6).
The fee on record is $6.61 with no surge applied (F7, F8), so there is no overcharge component to strike down beyond the cancellation fee itself.

The rider cancelled after writing "Sorry, plans changed, I will cancel" (F10), a voluntary change of mind rather than a driver failure, and the chat record is complete with every message timestamped (F9, F11), so there is no missing-record gap that would send the fee question to a human adjudicator.

The driver's post-trip statement that he "was parked at the pickup for minutes" (F12) is corroborated, not contradicted, by the GPS and timeline (F3: stationary 4 min 40 s, 41 m from pickup), so it adds nothing to the rider's case.
The driver has 2 upheld no-show disputes in 90 days (F17) and the rider 1 dispute, 0 upheld (F16); these history facts are background only and are not a basis for refusing or granting this fee.

weaknesses: Timing is against us: the rider cancelled 6 min 40 s after matching, well past NS-4's 3-minute free-cancellation window (F4), and NS-4 gives no relief for a driver who has not yet arrived - the record shows the driver was already within 200 m from 08:41:25 (F2).

The rider's own message "Sorry, plans changed, I will cancel" (F10) is an admission that the cancellation was the rider's choice, and the complete, timestamped chat (F11) leaves no missing-record gap to push the fee question to a human adjudicator.

The driver's 2 upheld no-show findings in 90 days (F17) and the rider's clean 90-day record (F16) are the only facts that could support a discretionary write-off, and profile facts cannot alone decide the case.

claims.assertion: This is a rider-cancelled instant booking (F4: accepted 08:40:00, cancelled by rider at 08:46:40, 6 min 40 s after matching), so the fee can only stand under NS-0's rider branch, i.e. NS-4, and the driver's arrival timeline does not by itself create a no-show charge.

Under NS-4 a rider cancellation is free only within 3 minutes of matching; the cancellation here came at 6 min 40 s, past that grace period, so NS-4 on its own makes the $6.61 cancellation fee stand (F4).

The rider's stated reason - plans changed and the driver not arrived - does not found a waiver: the record shows the driver was within 200 m of the pickup from 08:41:25 and stationary 41 m away from 08:42:00 (F2, F3).

The only ground on which the $6.61 could be refunded is a defect in the driver's arrival/waiting record, and that ground fails: the driver tapped "I'm Here" at 08:42:15 while 40 m from the pickup (within the 200 m arrival radius), stayed within 200 m for 4 min 25 s after the tap, and the cancellation came 5 min 15 s after arrival, more than 3 minutes (F2, F5, F6).
The fee on record is $6.61 with no surge applied (F7, F8), so there is no overcharge component to strike down beyond the cancellation fee itself.

The rider cancelled after writing "Sorry, plans changed, I will cancel" (F10), a voluntary change of mind rather than a driver failure, and the chat record is complete with every message timestamped (F9, F11), so there is no missing-record gap that would send the fee question to a human adjudicator.

The driver's post-trip statement that he "was parked at the pickup for minutes" (F12) is corroborated, not contradicted, by the GPS and timeline (F3: stationary 4 min 40 s, 41 m from pickup), so it adds nothing to the rider's case.
The driver has 2 upheld no-show disputes in 90 days (F17) and the rider 1 dispute, 0 upheld (F16); these history facts are background only and are not a basis for refusing or granting this fee.

weaknesses: Timing is against us: the rider cancelled 6 min 40 s after matching, well past NS-4's 3-minute free-cancellation window (F4), and NS-4 gives no relief for a driver who has not yet arrived - the record shows the driver was already within 200 m from 08:41:25 (F2).

The arrival record is clean on its face: "I'm Here" tapped at 08:42:15 while 40 m from pickup, 4 min 25 s within 200 m afterwards, and cancellation 5 min 15 s after arrival (F5, F6), so NS-1 (i)(ii)(iii) appear satisfied and NS-2's refund trigger is not engaged; the other side will cite exactly these facts.

The rider's own message "Sorry, plans changed, I will cancel" (F10) is an admission that the cancellation was the rider's choice, and the complete, timestamped chat (F11) leaves no missing-record gap to push the fee question to a human adjudicator.

The driver's 2 upheld no-show findings in 90 days (F17) and the rider's clean 90-day record (F16) are the only facts that could support a discretionary write-off, and profile facts cannot alone decide the case.

claims.assertion: The rider cancelled this trip herself at 08:46:40, 6 min 40 s after acceptance, so the $6.61 must be assessed under NS-0 via the rider-cancellation branch for an on-demand trip (NS-4), not the no-show branch.
The rider cancelled more than 3 minutes after matching (6 min 40 s), and the $6.61 was on record, so under NS-4 the cancellation fee stands and no refund is due.

Independently of who cancelled, the driver had already reached the pickup: first within 200 m at 08:41:25 and stationary 41 m from the pickup point for 4 min 40 s, so the rider's claim that 'the driver had not even arrived' is contradicted by the GPS record.

The driver tapped 'I'm Here' at 08:42:15 while 40 m from the pickup point and remained within 200 m for 4 min 25 s thereafter until cancellation, so even on the strict no-show standard the driver complied with the arrival and waiting requirements.
The rider's own message at 08:45, 'Sorry, plans changed, I will cancel', shows the cancellation was caused by the rider's changed plans, not by any driver fault or unavailability.
The chat record is complete and fully timestamped (2 messages), so no inference of missing evidence should be drawn against the driver (G12 concerns only incomplete records).
The driver's own statement that he was parked at the pickup for minutes is corroborated by the GPS stationary period, so it does not conflict with any system record.
There is no traffic, weather or route disturbance in the record that could have prevented the driver from being ready at the pickup, so nothing external excuses the rider's late cancellation.

No safety issue arises on this record: the only chat content is a neutral arrival notice and a polite rider apology, with no threat, harassment or dangerous-driving allegation, and no accident, injury or vehicle incident is recorded.

The driver's history (2 upheld no-show disputes in 90 days) is not the basis of this decision and no flag_account is sought here, because this cancellation was rider-initiated and the driver met the arrival and waiting requirements.

weaknesses: The trip was never started and the driver incurred no driving cost for it; the rider cancelled 5 min 15 s after the driver arrived but only 6 min 40 s after acceptance, and a judge may treat a short wait at the pickup as weak grounds for a full $6.61 fee — the rider will cite F4 (6 min 40 s) and F9. Also, this fee is imposed on an on-demand trip (RydeX, per the trip header) by NS-4 alone; the driver's arrival evidence F2/F3/F6 is not in fact needed to sustain it, so the judge may discount it.

The driver tapped 'I'm Here' (F6) only 50 s after the platform had already recorded arrival (F5, 08:41:25); the rider may argue the tap was premature and that the driver was still stationary at 41 m from the pickup (F3) rather than at the exact pickup point, though 41 m is within the 200 m data-layer radius used for NS-1 (ii).

The driver's 90-day record shows 2 no-show disputes, both upheld (F17); although the rider in this case cancelled and the fee is sustained on the rider's own timing (F4), the judge could be influenced by that pattern, and the rider's clean record (F16, 0 upheld) is not a rule but is an appeal-to-fairness point.
